reason: The completed DSX 32K Q173 result showed raw pp_throughput of 880311 tok/s while first content-token E2E latency was 55.9–148.0 s. Inspection of llama-benchy 0.4.0 source confirms pp_throughput uses est_ppt = first-SSE-chunk time minus a network probe; a role-only SSE chunk can arrive before model prefill completes. The raw metric is therefore invalid for this server response pattern.
changes: Retain all original benchy JSON and event files unchanged.

For Q190 comparisons, compute per-request effective prefill TPS as request_end.prompt_tokens / request_first_token.ttft_s, i.e. actual prompt tokens divided by request-start-to-first-content-token time.

Report the mean of per-request rates per context, n, and sample standard deviation. Label it effective end-to-end prefill; it includes client/network overhead and remains comparable between the matched profiles.

Treat llama-benchy pp_throughput and est_ppt as diagnostic-only where first SSE response is materially earlier than the first content-bearing token; do not use them for the decision or Sheet macro average.

Apply the calculation to the already completed DSX 32K n=3 using retained progress events, then use the amended runner for remaining DSX and Maya contexts. No repeat is needed for the 32K samples because request token counts and first-content-token times are present in the immutable event trace.
Decode TPS remains the native Q173 tg_throughput metric, after confirming exact 128-token completion and zero per-request errors.

source_evidence.first_response_semantics: first chunk of any kind; may be empty/role-only
